comparator.name: Biomedische wetenschappen
comparator.academicYear: Current curriculum for the 2026–27 cohort; checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: Official prospective and current-student curriculum pages establish a 180-EC degree with a 135-EC major and 45-EC profiling space. The major comprises 75 EC of required study and 60 EC of major-bound choice: seven 7.5-EC first-year compulsory courses, one 7.5-EC first-year biomedical elective, 15 EC Onderzoeksmethoden, 7.5 EC Bio-informatica, five 7.5-EC advanced major-bound electives including Moleculaire Biologie van de Cel, and the compulsory 15-EC Researchproject. The 2026–27 concept curriculum confirms exceptional component sizes. No formal named graduation route is required, so no route is imposed. The prospective site separately announces a redesigned curriculum only from September 2027.
components: One biomedical elective is chosen from the published first-year green list; the choice remains neutral rather than inventing a specialisation.
Five of ten published major-bound electives are required, including Moleculaire Biologie van de Cel; this variable space remains open.
Compulsory third-year literature study plus experimental research or mini-internship and thesis.
Open profiling space; no optional minor or other named route is imposed.

core: Molecular, cellular, biochemical and genetic mechanisms of human health and disease
Human anatomy, physiology, tissues and organ-system function
Disease mechanisms, cancer, infection and immunity
Biomedical research, laboratory methods, statistics, bioinformatics and data
Translation from biomedical research to diagnosis, treatment and clinical medicine
Ethical, societal and communication dimensions of biomedical impact
adjacent: Neuroscience, cognition and behaviour as human biomedical systems
Population health, prevention and environmental health risk
Computational and quantitative analysis of biomedical evidence
questions: How do molecular, cellular and genetic processes cause disease?
How are biomedical discoveries translated into diagnosis and treatment?
How can cancer, infection and other major health problems be understood and prevented?

candidates.label: Molecular genetics, cancer and biomedical data

alternatives.label: Human biology, disease and biomedical research
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule follows the comparator's molecules-to-organism biomedical core, disease mechanisms, laboratory and quantitative research, translation and societal impact.
alternatives.concept: A broad biomedical-sciences programme spanning molecular and cellular mechanisms, physiology, anatomy, infection, disease, pharmacology, public health and research methods.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes all dependent HCB work; mathematical and statistical foundations precede advanced quantitative study. Laboratory, molecular, physiological and research-method courses progress from introductory to advanced level, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Molecular genetics, cancer and biomedical data
alternatives.labelReason: Direct interests in molecular and cellular illness and genetics support a computationally stronger biomedical route centred on pathology, cancer-relevant disease mechanisms and research data.
alternatives.concept: A molecular and cellular biomedical programme strengthened with programming, imaging, data management, machine learning and quantitative modelling.
progression: Programming and mathematical foundations precede advanced data science; Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes all dependent HCB courses. Molecular Cell Biology, Biochemistry and laboratory work precede advanced pathology and disease courses, and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces Epidemiology & Public Health, Neurobiology, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Functional Anatomy, Ethics and Medical & Health Psychology with Programming, Image Processing, Deep Learning, Database Management, Machine Learning and Psycholinguistics. The resulting programme is substantially more computational and data-centred while retaining its molecular biomedical core.

alternatives.label: Physiology, infection and translational health
alternatives.labelReason: Direct interests in diagnosis, treatment, biomedical research and clinical medicine support a human-systems route combining physiology, infection, disease and psychological diagnosis and therapy.
alternatives.concept: A human-centred biomedical programme combining anatomy and physiology, molecular pathology, infection and immunity, disease mechanisms, pharmacology, diagnosis, treatment and developmental health.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior precede dependent biomedical, cognitive and psychology courses. Molecular, physiological and methods courses develop before advanced disease, pharmacology, diagnosis and treatment work, and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Probability & Statistics and Natural Hazards with Abnormal Psychology, Free Will, Time & the Self, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies and Lifespan Developmental Psychology. The result shifts from broad quantitative and population-risk coverage toward clinical diagnosis, treatment and lifespan health.

blocks: Both establish cellular and molecular foundations for human biomedical study.
Both develop molecular cell biology and biochemical mechanisms.
Both connect molecular processes and genetic information, with the explicit genome focus reinforced by Molecular Pathology & Genetics.
Both connect molecular and genetic change to disease, including cancer-relevant mechanisms.
Both integrate human physiology at organism and organ-system level.
Functional anatomy complements the comparator's tissues and organism structure.
Both connect biomedical knowledge to prevention and wider health impact.
UCR laboratory work supplies hands-on experimental practice within the comparator's broader compulsory methods component.
The advanced seminar provides research design, analysis and scholarly synthesis, but not the comparator's compulsory 15-EC thesis project.
Both develop quantitative data literacy; the comparator specifically applies it to biological information.
The first-year biomedical elective remains neutral.
The five advanced major-bound electives remain variable rather than being forced into one fictitious route.
The 45-EC profiling space remains open and is not treated as fixed comparator content.

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the programme's full biomedical core. Two direct interest clusters support coherent and substantially distinct alternatives: molecular/genetic biomedical data, and physiology/infection/translational health. Each schedule contains 24 feasible current UCR courses, the alternatives differ by at least four courses, and production stops at the maximum of three defensible alternatives.

notes.text: Utrecht Biomedical Sciences has a prescribed 135-EC major, a compulsory 15-EC Researchproject and a large published biomedical elective catalogue. UCR can build strong biomedical pathways from molecular, physiological, disease, public-health and quantitative courses, but it does not reproduce Utrecht's dedicated Researchproject or every specialist elective; shared rows indicate substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
